claims.explanation: PD-407824 is annotated as a WEE1 inhibitor, and its selective killing pattern is best explained by loss of G1/S checkpoint control (e.g., TP53 mutation) combined with intact replication stress responses, which forces cells to rely on WEE1 for survival. The virtual cell response shows strong induction of p53 targets (GADD45A, SESN1, PMAIP1) and downregulation of replication genes (MCM3, PCNA, TOP2A), consistent with DNA damage and replication stress. Thus, tumors with defective p53 and additional lesions in PI3K/RTK/RAS or chromatin remodeling are most sensitive, whereas those with intact p53 or alternative survival pathways are protected.

features.basis: Loss of G1/S checkpoint increases reliance on WEE1; TP53 mutations are highly enriched in sensitive lines.
High WEE1 expression would counteract the drug's inhibitory effect and protect cells.
High cyclin A2 drives replication stress; virtual cell shows CCNA2 downregulation upon treatment.
Active CDK1 is required for WEE1 dependency; high CDK1 activity sensitizes to WEE1 inhibition.
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT, increasing replication stress and sensitivity; seen in several sensitive lines.
PIK3CA mutations are present in multiple sensitive lines and may enhance replication stress.
KRAS mutations drive proliferation and replication stress; observed in sensitive lines.
BRAF mutations are common in sensitive melanoma lines and may increase replication stress.
ATM loss impairs DNA damage response, increasing reliance on WEE1; seen in sensitive lines.
CHK1 is a key checkpoint kinase; high expression may compensate for WEE1 inhibition.
ATR pathway activity can compensate for WEE1 loss; high ATR may protect cells.
High MCM3 indicates replication licensing; virtual cell shows MCM3 downregulation upon treatment.
